#399 implement.summary:
I committed #399 as one commit, 1b098733, on fix/399-extension-select-shows-the-whole-title in /tmp/wt-399, on top of main 8f7d98aa. It is not pushed. Codex cross-review was not run in this lane.

What changed:
- The select title, and the confirm title and message, now wrap like pi's. They reuse approval_dialog's _shown, _cut and _ansi_named rather than copies. A control character is drawn by name in reverse video (CR as ^M, ESC as ^[).
- A new control, _TitleHeldControl in tui/context.py, draws both dialogs. A title drawn whole is never held.
- When a title is taller than the room it gets, it scrolls in the approval prompt's _BodyViewport, with the same footer and PgUp/PgDn. Every option (Enter, Space and Ctrl+J in select; y in confirm) waits until every title row has been drawn. Esc, Ctrl+C and n always answer.
- The title is never withheld to make room. If even the option rows do not fit, a title that fits is drawn whole and the rows below it are cut as before. A title taller than the whole modal gets half of it.
- Text from an extension or the model is the default: an approving key typed before the first paint is dropped, and the option rows stay on screen while the title scrolls. That default covers ctx.ui, the permission fallback and spawn consent; the latter two carry comments saying they pass no own on purpose.
- aelix's own pickers pass own=True and keep their old layout and pre-paint behaviour. This covers /resume, theme, /settings, /trust and the session-in-use prompt directly, and /model, /thinking, /login and /logout through functools.partial.
- consent.py: the 300-character task cut and the 68-character Directory: middle elision are gone. Source: keeps its elision, and the batch rows keep their 72-character cut.
- Docs: ADR-0253 section 11.3, the ADR-0199 status line plus a dated note in its section (c), README rows 0253 and 0199, the extension-authoring guide and its bundled copy, and a CHANGELOG Security entry.

The main loop's kit is /Users/handochan/dev/aelix-ai/.omc/probes/399-live/impl/kit/run_live.sh, with the groups gates, consent and pickers. To compare against base it needs a worktree at 8f7d98aa; the script header says how to create it.

owner_decisions: How the calls are marked: an extension's ctx.ui reaches AelixTUIContext.select itself, so the hold is the default and aelix's own pickers are the ones marked (own=True). A picker I missed would drop a key typed before its first paint instead of taking it, which errs on the safe side. The alternative is a proxy bound for extensions.

Layout: an extension's or the model's title that would fit whole but push its options off screen now scrolls, so the options stay visible. aelix's own pickers keep the old layout. As a result, /trust at 80x16 now wraps its whole disclosure and loses 'Do not trust', the counter and the hint off the bottom of the modal (Esc still answers). Marking /trust as non-own would scroll it and hold Enter instead.
Every option row is held, including literal 'Cancel' or 'No' rows; Esc and Ctrl+C are the keys that always answer. Exempting labelled refusals would need a new parameter.

Wrapping the uncut Directory or task lets a model lay text out to look like a row at a known width (for example a flattened 'Permission: plan' inside the Directory row breaking at column 80). It cannot hide the real rows, which are always drawn after it.
The 72-character batch member cut and the Source: elision are kept, because the decision named only the 300 cut and the 68 Directory elision.
follow_ups: LoginContext (an extension login provider's select and confirm) should get the default held select and confirm, not aelix's own=True partial.
Spawn consent batch: member tasks are still cut at 72 characters (BATCH_TASK_PREVIEW_CHARS). Show whole members and hold, or keep the cut on purpose and document it.
Wrapped title rows could carry a hanging indent or continuation marker so a model cannot align text to look like a row of its own (Directory or task in consent).
The pre-TUI one-shot selector in cli/entry.py has no height cap or hold: a body taller than the terminal cuts its options, and a key typed before paint is taken.
/agents run as the first command of a fresh session takes the clamp without a dialog. This is documented in _host_consent_context but surprising; the live kit needs a prompt first.
pyte draws pi's '⚠️ Dangerous command:' row as just the ⚠ on both base and fix (VS16). Check it in a real terminal.

blocking.title: An extension title that fits the modal is scrolled to make room for its options, against decision 2
blocking.detail: For untrusted dialogs, _TitleHeldControl._layout counts a title as whole only when title_count + needed <= height. Otherwise it scrolls the title in the rows left over after the options, even when the title alone fits the modal. Example: a 5-row extension question with 8 options in the 80x16 modal (11 rows) shows 1 of 5 title rows, holds Enter, and needs 4 PgDn. 8f7d98aa draws all 5 rows and cuts options from the bottom. Decision 2 says a fully drawn title is never held and the title is never withheld to make room; when the dialog cannot fit, rows below are cut or the options area scrolls. ADR-0253 §11.3 lists this choice ('How much room ... the modal less the rule and the option rows') under 'Decision (owner)'. It needs rework or the owner's sign-off, plus a fix to that attribution.
blocking.evidence: kit/room_probe.py: out/room_probe.txt (F at 80x11: 'title rows drawn 1/5, Enter answered at once=False ... answered after 4 PgDn'; at 80x13: 3/5) vs out/room_probe_base.txt (B: 5/5, answered at once). The lane's test test_an_extension_title_scrolls_so_its_options_stay_on_screen pins this behaviour.
